The reports concluded that there existed a "significant opportunity to improve sales through better targeting." "Better targeting" meant focusing sales calls on extreme high-volume opioid prescribers and removing sales representative discretion with respect to call plans.
context: Settlement describes how Purdue rebranded intensive targeting of high-volume prescribers with aspirational terminology.

label: Value decile analysis enhancing prescriber focus
original_label: Value decile analysis enhancing prescriber focus
quote: The consulting company contended that, in contrast to the decile ranking undertaken by Purdue from 2010 to 2012, its rankings focused on "value deciles," which purported to be qualitatively different. In practice, the value decile ranking only enhanced Purdue's marketing focus on extreme high-volume prescribers and ensured a focus on Federal healthcare program beneficiaries. The "value decile" analysis purported to use the following metrics: (1) overall opioid prescriptions, including number of branded versus generic prescriptions; (2) whether the prescriber had rules in place prohibiting sales representatives from calling on them; (3) managed care access, including access to Federal healthcare program beneficiaries; and (4) the number of the prescriber's new to brand prescriptions (including new opioid patients and switches from other opioid products).
context: Settlement describes how Purdue disguised continued high-volume prescriber targeting as a methodological innovation using neutral technical terminology.

label: Indirect pharmacy calls on Region Zero prescribers
original_label: Indirect pharmacy calls on Region Zero prescribers
quote: To ensure that prescriptions from extreme high-volume prescribers would be filled, Purdue engaged in certain strategies, including instructing its sales representatives to detail pharmacies and paying kickbacks to specialty pharmacies to fill red flag prescriptions, which is discussed further below. Purdue also sought to encourage the pharmacists to "reach out to a Prescriber to recommend that a patient be switched from immediate release oxycodone to OxyContin." In other words, Purdue's pharmacy calls both functioned to assuage pharmacists' concerns about filling prescriptions for OxyContin and at times served as a proxy or indirect call on the very Region Zero prescribers Purdue allegedly precluded the sales force from directly contacting.
context: Settlement describes how Purdue used neutral pharmacy calls as euphemistic workaround to indirectly target prescribers supposedly removed from direct sales calls.

label: Speaker programs and advisory boards as kickbacks
original_label: Speaker programs and advisory boards as kickbacks
quote: As an additional means to induce doctors to prescribe Purdue's opioid drugs, from 2010 through at least March 2018, Purdue paid kickbacks to certain prescribers in the form of speaker programs, advisory board memberships, research programs and honoraria. Purdue allowed its sales and marketing personnel, who had data on each doctor's prescribing of Purdue's drugs and whose compensation depended on increasing their assigned doctors' prescribing of Purdue's drugs, to select speakers instead of Purdue's medical education staff.
context: Settlement describes how Purdue disguised payments designed to induce prescriptions using legitimate-sounding scientific and educational terminology.

label: 80 mg tablet decline among suspected prescribers
original_label: 80 mg tablet decline among suspected prescribers
quote: Among the Board materials was a presentation stating that there was a "[d]ecline in 80 mg prescriptions, esp[ecially] among 'Do not Call' prescribers," and a "[s]hift in routes of abuse, especially injecting and snorting." The study, which surveyed individuals being treated for opioid use disorder who reported abusing OxyContin through any route, also found that while the overall rate of OxyContin abuse decreased, some users continued to abuse Reformulated OxyContin through insufflation or injection—albeit with more difficulty—and that the percentage of users who reported abusing OxyContin through oral ingestion increased from 54% to 76% following the introduction of Reformulated OxyContin.
context: Board presentation treats the decline in 80 mg prescriptions from suspected abusers as merely a shift in routes rather than as an indication that removed prescribers were engaging in abuse.

label: Consulting company identified E2E opportunities
original_label: Consulting company identified E2E opportunities
quote: On August 23, 2013, certain Sackler family members met with the consulting company and examined its "unvarnished" findings and recommendations. Following the meeting, one of the consulting company partners that led the meeting with the Sacklers memorialized in an email: "[T]he room was filled with only family, including the elder statesman Dr. Raymond [Sackler]. . . . We went through exhibit by exhibit for about 2 hrs. . . . They were extremely supportive of the findings and our recommendations . . . and wanted to strongly endorse getting going on our recommendations."
context: Settlement recounts how Sackler family could cite consulting company recommendations as independent strategic guidance while maintaining full authority and approval.

label: Board pressure on executives for growth targets
original_label: Board pressure on executives for growth targets
quote: On January 25, 2010, Richard Sackler emailed the Board and informed them that he had "engaged management on this subject," referring to the proposed 2010 budget, and explained his view that management's number was "unduly conservative." On the same day, Mortimer D.A. Sackler followed up with Theresa Sackler regarding Richard's proposal, stating "we should push management to agree to a higher target."
context: Settlement describes how Board members including Sacklers pressured management on sales targets while appearing to displace responsibility for achieving them to management.

label: Prescriber failure to titrate patients appropriately
original_label: Prescriber failure to titrate patients appropriately
quote: For example, a 2011 script stated: "We discussed the discontinuation rate of extended-release opioids by day 35. One of the potential reasons for discontinuation is the lack of efficacy perhaps as a result of lack of titration." E2E created a refreshed 2014 version of the script that stated: "According to an analysis … 57% of patients initiated on some commonly prescribed extended-release opioids are no longer on those products by day 35," "Assuming a patient discontinues therapy by day 35 due to their perceived lack of pain relief, what is the impact on your patient, you and your staff? (pause for effect)," and then "Doctor, working with you and your staff, I can provide support to you when initiating and titrating dosages on my products."
context: Sales script frames patient discontinuation of opioids as a failure of physician titration rather than as successful patient rejection of inappropriate medication.

label: Specialty pharmacies fill rejected prescriptions
original_label: Specialty pharmacies fill rejected prescriptions
quote: From mid-2015 through 2018, the specialty pharmacies filled Medicare prescriptions for Purdue opioids written by approximately 100 prescribers. Nearly one-fourth of those prescribers were referred to ADD on suspicion of engaging in abuse and diversion. Some of the prescriptions that were filled by the specialty pharmacies had been rejected by traditional retail pharmacies and displayed indicia that the prescriptions were not for a medically accepted indication; for uses that were unsafe, ineffective, and medically unnecessary; and that were often diverted for uses that lacked a legitimate medical purpose.
context: Settlement presents data showing that specialty pharmacies filled prescriptions from prescribers with abuse-diversion flags, without treating this as evidence of harm.

label: Increased government scrutiny as market headwind
original_label: Increased government scrutiny as market headwind
quote: Purdue also attributed approximately 40% of the decline in OxyContin prescriptions in 2010 to 2011 to "Region Zero" prescribers. Purdue attributed the remainder of the sales decline, in large part, to both the reformulation and safeguards against medically unnecessary prescriptions. A consulting company that worked for Purdue since approximately the mid-2000s similarly attributed the decline in sales, in large part, to both the reformulation and safeguards against medically unnecessary prescriptions. In 2013, the consulting company informed Purdue and its Board, that "[t]he retail channel, both pharmacies and distributors, is under intense scrutiny and direct risk."
context: Purdue and its consultants characterize government safeguards against medically unnecessary prescribing as business challenges to be overcome rather than as legitimate public health measures.

category: Appeal to legality and technical compliance
label: FDA-approved label governs appropriate use
original_label: FDA-approved label governs appropriate use
quote: OxyContin is approved by HHS's Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the management of pain severe enough to require daily, around-the-clock, long-term opioid treatment and for which alternative treatment options are inadequate.
context: Settlement repeatedly cites FDA approval as establishing legitimate use parameters, implicitly treating regulatory approval as settling the ethics question.

category: Appeal to legality and technical compliance
label: Andersen audit opinion and GAAP compliance defense
original_label: Andersen audit opinion and GAAP compliance defense
quote: When confronted by evidence of Enron's high risk accounting, all of the Board members interviewed by the Subcommittee pointed out that Enron's auditor, Andersen, had given the company a clean audit opinion each year. None recalled any occasion on which Andersen had expressed any objection to a particular transaction or accounting practice at Enron, despite evidence indicating that, internally at Andersen, concerns about Enron's accounting were commonplace. But a failure by Andersen to object does not preclude a finding that the Enron Board, with Andersen's concurrence, knowingly allowed Enron to use high risk accounting and failed in its fiduciary duty to ensure the company engaged in responsible financial reporting.
context: The investigative report describes how Board members relied on Andersen's clean audit opinion and technical compliance as justification for not questioning Enron's high-risk accounting practices.

category: Appeal to legality and technical compliance
label: Board members claim reliance on GAAP and professional approval
original_label: Board members claim reliance on GAAP and professional approval
quote: Lord Wakeham, a chartered accountant and chairman of an audit committee at another company, said that Enron was engaged in business transactions that had not been done by many companies in the world and were relatively new. He indicated that he believed Enron's practices were within the bounds of generally accepted accounting principles since they had been approved by Andersen. He told the Subcommittee staff that he had believed Andersen would stand by their accounting advice and was shocked when, in 2001, Andersen began to reverse course and repudiate the accounting methodologies and judgments it had earlier provided.
context: A Board member justifies reliance on Andersen's technical approval of accounting practices to deflect responsibility for failing to question high-risk transactions.

label: Board relies on management and auditor representations without verification
original_label: Board relies on management and auditor representations without verification
quote: The Subcommittee investigation did not substantiate the claims that the Enron Board members challenged management and asked tough questions. Instead, the investigation found a Board that routinely relied on Enron management and Andersen representations with little or no effort to verify the information provided, that readily approved new business ventures and complex transactions, and that exercised weak oversight of company operations.
context: The investigative report characterizes how Board members displaced responsibility by relying on expert assurances from Andersen and management rather than conducting independent verification.

label: Board defers to Andersen on high-risk accounting judgment
original_label: Board defers to Andersen on high-risk accounting judgment
quote: Mr. Duncan reviewed Enron's 1998 financial statements, audit and internal controls. The minutes state that Mr. Duncan then reviewed selected observations by Arthur Andersen including a risk profile analysis of accounting judgements, disclosure judgements, and rule changes. He was joined in the discussion by Mr. Bauer. In connection with its risk profile of Enron, Andersen provided Audit Committee members with a one-page document entitled, Selected Observations 1998 Financial Reporting. This document identified four accounting issues at Enron: Highly Structured Transactions, Commodity and Equity Portfolio, Purchase Accounting, and Balance Sheet Issues, three of which also had subissues. Each issue was followed by a Risk Profile table with three headings: Accounting Judgements, Disclosure Judgements, and Rule Changes. The table then assigned an H, M, or L rating to each element of the Risk Profile. In short, on February 7, 1999, Andersen informed the Audit Committee members that Enron was engaged in accounting practices that push limits or were at the edge of acceptable practice. In the discussion that followed, Andersen did not advocate any change in company practice, and no Board member objected to Enron's actions, requested a second opinion of Enron's accounting practices, or demanded a more prudent approach.
context: The Audit Committee received explicit warnings from Andersen about high-risk accounting marked with H ratings but took no independent action, instead accepting Andersen's framing that the practices were acceptable.

label: Board assumes management approval equals adequate oversight
original_label: Board assumes management approval equals adequate oversight
quote: The interviewed Board members told the Subcommittee staff that, after the October 2000 meeting in which the Finance Committee was told that Mr. Causey, Mr. Buy, and Mr. Skilling would approve all Enron-LJM transactions, they assumed Mr. Skilling was actively reviewing the Enron-LJM transactions. Mr. Skilling testified at a House hearing, however, that he had been unaware of any obligation to review the LJM transactions and did not, as a matter of course, review them for fairness or sign the relevant documents.
context: Board members displaced responsibility by assuming management had put controls in place, when in fact the designated managers had not actively implemented them.

label: Board delegates compensation oversight to consultant
original_label: Board delegates compensation oversight to consultant
quote: Dr. LeMaistre testified that he did not worry about high levels of compensation because he checked regularly with the Board's compensation consultant, Towers Perrin, and was informed that Enron was right on target in its compensation practices.
context: A Board member uses reliance on a compensation consultant as justification for not exercising direct oversight of executive compensation levels.

label: Winokur claims concealment of problems
original_label: Winokur claims concealment of problems
quote: Mr. Winokur, former head of the Finance Committee, testified that Enron was a cautionary reminder of the limits of a director's role which is by nature a part-time job. He stated, We cannot, I submit, be criticized for failing to address or remedy problems that have been concealed from us.
context: A senior Board member deflects responsibility by asserting that the Board cannot be faulted for problems hidden from them.

label: Duncan blames management and Andersen for concealment
original_label: Duncan blames management and Andersen for concealment
quote: John Duncan, former Executive Committee Chairman, testified that the Board worked hard and asked probing questions. He said the problem at Enron was that Enron management did not tell the truth, and both management and Andersen personnel were well aware of the problems facing the company and they did not tell us.
context: A Board witness deflects responsibility by claiming management and auditors deliberately withheld critical information from the Board.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: Board members deny awareness of Fastow's massive LJM compensation
original_label: Board members deny awareness of Fastow's massive LJM compensation
quote: A number of Board members claimed that the Board had been misled or misinformed regarding key aspects of the LJM partnerships. For example, Board members said they were not told how many Enron employees held ownership interests in LJM, how much time Enron employees were spending on LJM deals as representatives of LJM, how many deals LJM had underway with Enron, how the deals were being negotiated, and how much profit LJM was making at Enron's expense.
context: Board members collectively deny personal knowledge or involvement in monitoring LJM arrangements, diffusing responsibility across the organization and claiming they lacked information.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: Compensation Committee members deny responsibility for monitoring CEO credit line
original_label: Compensation Committee members deny responsibility for monitoring CEO credit line
quote: At the hearing, when Dr. LeMaistre, former Compensation Committee Chairman, was asked whether his Committee should have been monitoring the credit line, he testified that, We never had any responsibility to monitor this. When asked whether he would agree that Mr. Lay had abused his credit line, Dr. LeMaistre testified that it was not a term I care to use and that he would stop short of characterizing Mr. Lay's actions as an abuse because I do not know the circumstances.
context: Compensation Committee leadership denies personal responsibility for oversight of the CEO's personal credit arrangements, diffusing accountability.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: Compensation Committee unaware of total bonuses paid
original_label: Compensation Committee unaware of total bonuses paid
quote: During their interviews, the Compensation Committee and other Board members indicated that they had been unaware of the total amount of bonuses paid in early 2001 for work performed in 2000. That year, Enron executives received about 430 million in annual bonuses under Enron's normal bonus plan. In addition, in exchange for meeting certain stock performance targets, a special program called the Performance Unit Plan paid bonuses to about 65 Enron executives totaling another 320 million. Board members indicated that they had been unaware that the company had paid out almost 750 million in cash bonuses for a year in which the company's entire net income was 975 million. Apparently, no one on the Compensation Committee had ever added up the numbers.
context: Multiple Board members claim collective ignorance of the cumulative impact of compensation decisions, diffusing personal responsibility for the aggregate cash drain.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: Audit Committee members deny knowledge of Andersen's concerns
original_label: Audit Committee members deny knowledge of Andersen's concerns
quote: Enron Board members told the Subcommittee staff that they had been unaware of any tensions between Andersen and Enron and unaware of the many concerns Andersen had with Enron's accounting practices. The interviewed Board members said that they had not been informed and were unaware of a February 2001 visit paid by the head of Andersen, Joseph Berardino, to Enron's headquarters and did not know why the meeting took place or what was discussed. They also said they were unaware that, shortly after the visit, in March 2001, a senior Andersen partner, Carl Bass, was removed from his Enron oversight role at Enron's request.
context: Audit Committee members claim uniformly to have lacked awareness of significant tensions and high-level Andersen actions, diffusing personal responsibility for auditor oversight.

label: Asset-light strategy and monetizing assets
original_label: Asset-light strategy and monetizing assets
quote: Another high profile strategy, referred to as making the company asset light, was aimed at shedding, or increasing immediate returns on, the company's capital-intensive energy projects like power plants that had traditionally been associated with low returns and persistent debt on the company's books. The goal was either to sell these assets outright or to sell interests in them to investors, and record the income as earnings which top Enron officials called monetizing or syndicating the assets.
context: Enron management used euphemistic language like 'asset light' and 'monetizing' to describe what was essentially moving assets off the balance sheet to disguise financial condition.

label: Off-balance-sheet vehicles and unconsolidated affiliates
original_label: Off-balance-sheet vehicles and unconsolidated affiliates
quote: The October 2000 presentation to the Finance Committee showed that one solution Enron had devised was to sell or syndicate its assets, not to independent third parties, but to unconsolidated affiliates—businesses like Whitewing, LJM, JEDI, the Hawaii 125-0 Trust and others that were not included in Enron's financial statements but were so closely associated with the company that Enron considered their assets to be part of Enron's own holdings.
context: Enron used the sanitized technical term 'unconsolidated affiliates' to describe special purpose entities designed to move Enron assets off its books.

label: Funds flow and balance sheet management
original_label: Funds flow and balance sheet management
quote: A presentation identifying 2 billion in past and planned Enron asset sales during 2000, primarily to LJM2 and two other unconsolidated affiliates, Whitewing and the Hawaii 125-0 Trust, is characterized as a 2000 Balance Sheet Management effort. Enron's 10 largest transactions in the second half of 2000 are described to the Finance Committee in terms of their balance sheet impact, producing Positive Funds Flow, Debt reduction, or Balance Sheet protection for the company.
context: Enron used euphemistic labels like 'Balance Sheet Management' and 'Funds Flow' to disguise transactions designed solely to improve financial statement appearance rather than achieve legitimate business objectives.

label: P&L hedges and P&L volatility transfer
original_label: P&L hedges and P&L volatility transfer
quote: One page states the purpose of the transaction: Establish a risk management program in order to hedge the Profit & Loss volatility of Enron investments. The next page discusses the Raptor transaction in terms of how it could provide P&L protection to Enron. A handwritten note taken by the Corporate Secretary during Committee consideration of the Raptors states: Does not transfer economic risk but transfers P&L volatility.
context: The Raptor transactions were presented and described using financial euphemisms suggesting legitimate hedging when the documents themselves admitted they did not transfer economic risk but only moved accounting volatility.

label: Related party footnote disclosure obfuscation
original_label: Related party footnote disclosure obfuscation
quote: Enron's initial public disclosures regarding its dealings with its unconsolidated affiliates such as JEDI, Whitewing, LJM, and the Raptor SPEs are nearly impossible to understand and difficult to reconcile with the transactions now known to have taken place. The Powers Report calls the disclosures fundamentally inadequate and castigates Enron for proxy statement and financial statement disclosures that fail to disclose facts that were important for an understanding of the substance of the transactions Enron entered into with related parties.
context: Enron deliberately used obfuscatory language and complex footnote structures to hide the substance and extent of related party transactions from investors.

label: Board downplays $710 million Raptor charge
original_label: Board downplays $710 million Raptor charge
quote: During their interviews, the Board members said that they first learned of the Raptor termination at an October 8, 2001 Board meeting, when Enron officers announced that the company had decided to terminate the Raptors and take an 800 million earnings charge. The final charge actually recorded on Enron's third quarter financial statement was about 710 million. The interviewed Board members indicated that they had not felt deep concern about the charge at the time, despite its size, because it was a one-time event. Most said that they had left the October meeting thinking that the company was still on track, and its earnings were strong enough to withstand the charge.
context: Board members minimized the significance of a massive $710 million earnings charge by characterizing it as a one-time event and claiming the company remained on track.

label: Board characterizes asset transfers as benign if disclosed
original_label: Board characterizes asset transfers as benign if disclosed
quote: When asked about Enron's extensive off-the-books activity, one of the Board members, Mr. Blake, stated during his interview that transferring assets off a company's books is not immoral as long as disclosed.
context: A Board member minimizes the harm of extensive off-the-books activity by suggesting disclosure alone would render it acceptable, ignoring the substantive impact on financial condition.

label: Board rejects Powers Committee self-critical findings
original_label: Board rejects Powers Committee self-critical findings
quote: During their interviews, all 13 Enron Board members strongly disagreed with the Powers Report conclusions that the Board had failed in its oversight duties. They contended that they had reasonably relied on assurances provided by Enron management, Andersen, and Vinson & Elkins, and had met their obligation to provide reasonable oversight of company operations. During the hearing, all five Board witnesses explicitly rejected any share of responsibility for Enron's collapse.
context: Board members uniformly rejected the Board's own special investigative committee's critical findings about Board oversight failures, defending their actions and condemning the investigation's conclusions.

label: Board members dismiss whistleblower warning as vague
original_label: Board members dismiss whistleblower warning as vague
quote: The October 2001 meeting was also when the Directors first learned of the Watkins' letter, although she was never identified by name to the Board, no Board member requested her identity, and the letter's strong warnings about the Raptors apparently were not disclosed to the outside directors. The interviewed directors said that Enron officers referred to the letter during the Board meeting as coming from an anonymous employee. They said it was discussed during an Audit Committee meeting first and then during the full Board meeting. The company's outside legal counsel, Vinson & Elkins, made the primary presentations and indicated that their preliminary investigation of the employee's concerns had found nothing worth further investigation.
context: Board members, through counsel's framing, discounted and delegitimized a whistleblower's detailed concerns by characterizing the matter as anonymous employee complaints that did not warrant investigation.

category: Moral justification and appeal to higher loyalties
label: Board philosophy of extraordinary rewards for extraordinary achievement
original_label: Board philosophy of extraordinary rewards for extraordinary achievement
quote: One Board member said during his interview that Enron's philosophy was to provide extraordinary rewards for extraordinary achievement; others claimed that the company was forced to provide lavish compensation to attract the best and brightest employees.
context: Board members justified approving massive executive compensation packages by appealing to a philosophy of rewarding top talent and maintaining competitive attractiveness.

label: Board relied on Vinson & Elkins legal review of LJM memorandum
original_label: Board relied on Vinson & Elkins legal review of LJM memorandum
quote: At the hearing, Mr. Winokur testified that the Finance Committee had been told that Enron's legal counsel, Vinson & Elkins, had reviewed the memorandum and relied on the law firm to alert the Board to any problems. He indicated that Vinson & Elkins never told the Board anything was amiss, which is why the Board never requested or reviewed the material.
context: The Finance Committee Chairman displaced responsibility by claiming reliance on outside counsel's review of LJM materials without independently verifying their accuracy.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: Board members deny knowledge of Southampton partnership
original_label: Board members deny knowledge of Southampton partnership
quote: A number of Board members claimed that the Board had been misled or misinformed regarding key aspects of the LJM partnerships. He and other Board members said that it was during the Powers investigation that they first learned of the Southampton partnership, which Mr. Fastow had established with five other Enron employees to invest in LJM1 and enabled these additional Enron employees to benefit financially at Enron's expense.
context: Board members claim they were unaware of the Southampton partnership, a key vehicle through which Enron employees benefited from LJM, diffusing personal responsibility for oversight.

label: Board delegates LJM approval controls to management
original_label: Board delegates LJM approval controls to management
quote: The Board relied on Enron management to develop and implement the day-to-day controls needed to monitor LJM, and limited its own oversight to less frequent and more generalized reviews. The nature and extent of the LJM controls actually put into place by Enron management varied over time. The original LJM1 presentation in June 1999 did not specify any controls. The LJM2 presentation in October 1999 specified just one control—that Chief Accounting Officer Richard Causey approve all transactions between Enron and LJM.
context: The Board displaced responsibility for LJM oversight by delegating implementation of controls to management and limiting its own role to periodic reviews.

label: Accounting practices described as cutting-edge innovation
original_label: Accounting practices described as cutting-edge innovation
quote: During their interviews, a number of Enron Board members stated that Enron was engaged in complex accounting and was operating in areas with few established accounting guidelines, but most declined to characterize Enron's accounting as high risk or aggressive. Mr. Blake characterized Enron as engaged in leading edge, not aggressive accounting.
context: A Board member reframed high-risk accounting that Andersen explicitly marked as risky as merely 'leading edge' to avoid the more accurate and alarming 'aggressive' or 'high-risk' characterization.

category: Appeal to legality and technical compliance
label: Mark-to-market accounting as GAAP-compliant practice
original_label: Mark-to-market accounting as GAAP-compliant practice
quote: In 1999, Audit Committee members were given a nine-page presentation on mark-to-market and fair value accounting issues, and told how Enron divisions were expanding their use of fair value accounting which require continuous revaluation of asset and liabilities on Enron's books.
context: The Board received presentations on mark-to-market accounting framed as a technical GAAP-compliant practice without critical examination of the judgment and estimates it required.

label: Whitewing characterized as off-balance-sheet vehicle
original_label: Whitewing characterized as off-balance-sheet vehicle
quote: A Finance Committee presentation in August 2000, for example, reported 561 million in Enron asset sales to Whitewing, with plans for additional sales of 389 million. Whitewing is described in the document as an [o]ff balance sheet vehicle to purchase assets from Enron. An Enron Deal Approval Sheet (DASH), given to Finance Committee members the same month reported refinancing Enron's interests in three power plants by selling them to Whitewing. This deal is explained as allowing Enron to keep the interests it holds in the assets through Whitewing off-blance sheet.
context: Whitewing was consistently labeled as an 'off-balance-sheet vehicle' in Board materials, using euphemistic language that sanitized what was essentially a structure to hide Enron assets.

label: Board assumes Causey and Buy reviewed LJM for fairness
original_label: Board assumes Causey and Buy reviewed LJM for fairness
quote: Mr. Causey and Mr. Buy have indicated that each reviewed the LJM transactions and signed the relevant documents, but considered only narrow procedural or risk issues; neither reviewed the transactions for their overall fairness to Enron.
context: The Board displaced responsibility by assuming that management signatories had reviewed LJM transactions for fairness, when in fact they reviewed only narrow procedural matters.

label: Board minimizes LJM risks despite huge returns and conflicts
original_label: Board minimizes LJM risks despite huge returns and conflicts
quote: Records indicate that LJM was a very profitable venture. Its 2000 annual partnership meeting report boasts of 23 investments with Enron and a 69 percent rate of return in its first year of operation, which Enron Board members with investment experience told the Subcommittee staff was a very high rate of return. These Board members observed that all of LJM's transactions with Enron had turned a profit for LJM, which they said was also unusual for an equity fund. According to LJM, some of the transactions, such as the Raptors, had produced returns as high as 2,500 percent.
context: Despite evidence of extraordinarily high and unusual returns that should have raised red flags about the fairness of LJM transactions, Board members did not demand additional scrutiny.

label: Compensation Committee member gives up on obtaining Fastow compensation data
original_label: Compensation Committee member gives up on obtaining Fastow compensation data
quote: Dr. LeMaistre, then Chairman of the Compensation Committee, was present at the Finance Committee meeting, and attempted to obtain the requested information on Mr. Fastow's LJM compensation. He indicated during his interview and at the hearing that, after the Finance Committee meeting, he asked Enron's senior compensation officer, Mary Joyce, to provide him with information on the outside income of all of Enron's 16(b) officers. He said that he did not specifically name Mr. Fastow to Ms. Joyce because he did not want to start any office gossip. Ms. Joyce did not provide him with the information he requested. He said that he asked her a second time to obtain the information, but she again did not do so. He admitted that he never actually named Mr. Fastow to her or insisted that she obtain information about his LJM compensation. Instead, Dr. LeMaistre let the matter drop.
context: A Committee chair displaced responsibility by asking for information in vague terms, accepting a denial of availability, and abandoning follow-up rather than directly insisting on getting the information he was tasked to obtain.

category: Appeal to legality and technical compliance
label: Audit Committee Chair defends reliance on Andersen advice
original_label: Audit Committee Chair defends reliance on Andersen advice
quote: During the hearing, Dr. Jaedicke, the former Audit Committee Chairman, said that [w]e knew that the company was engaged in high-risk and innovative transactions, but did not recall being told that the company's accounting practices push limits. He testified: David Duncan did tell us on several occasions that these were complex transactions, that they were complex structures, that Enron was a complex company. They were moving very fast, and very careful accounting judgments were required. I do not recall him saying, well, others could have a different view. But I think all of us understood that these were highly structured, new kinds of transactions, but Enron paid Arthur Andersen some pretty hefty fees, to try to be in on the beginning of these transactions so that those accounting judgments would be properly made.
context: The Audit Committee Chair justified reliance on Andersen's technical accounting judgments by noting the substantial fees paid to ensure proper professional judgment, treating financial compliance as settling the ethical question.

label: Prepays and FASB 125 sales as structured finance
original_label: Prepays and FASB 125 sales as structured finance
quote: Finance Committee presentations also alerted Board members to Enron's increasing use of Prepays and FASB 125 Sales, complex transactions that used sophisticated accounting rules to add billions of dollars to Enron's reported earnings and cash flow.
context: Enron used technical financial labels like 'Prepays' and 'FASB 125 Sales' to describe complex transactions that were in fact disguised loans designed to inflate financial statements.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: Board members claim they did not learn of 1.2 billion equity reduction
original_label: Board members claim they did not learn of 1.2 billion equity reduction
quote: During their interviews, the Directors were unanimous in stating that, while Enron disclosed the prospective 800 million earnings charge at the October 8 Board meeting, Enron management did not disclose at that meeting that the Raptors termination would also require a reduction in shareholder equity of 1.2 billion. Most of the Directors recalled learning of the 1.2 billion after a Wall Street Journal article quoted the figure following Mr. Lay's disclosure of it during a financial analyst call on October 17.
context: Multiple Board directors collectively claim ignorance of a $1.2 billion equity reduction until they learned of it from press coverage, diffusing responsibility for monitoring material financial impacts.

label: Related parties recharacterized as independent third parties
original_label: Related parties recharacterized as independent third parties
quote: The Board was told that LJM1 would be set up as a special purpose entity that would not be on Enron's balance sheet, and it would be owned in part and managed by Mr. Fastow. Its first transaction, which was presented to the Board for approval, involved a high tech stock called Rhythms NetConnections, which Enron had purchased at the company's initial public offering for 10 million and whose value had skyrocketed to about 300 million. Enron had already recognized the appreciation in the stock price as earnings on its financial statements, and wanted to protect its income statements from any loss if the stock price fell. The Board was told that, through a novel and complicated transaction, LJM1 could provide a hedge on the Rhythms stock at no cost to Enron.
context: LJM1, an entity owned and managed by Enron's CFO, was presented to the Board as capable of providing a hedge at no cost, obscuring the fundamental conflict of interest and the fact that the entity was not truly independent.

label: Audit Committee relies on Vinson & Elkins Raptor investigation
original_label: Audit Committee relies on Vinson & Elkins Raptor investigation
quote: The company's outside legal counsel, Vinson & Elkins, made the primary presentations and indicated that their preliminary investigation of the employee's concerns had found nothing worth further investigation. The interviewed directors said the employee's concerns were characterized as having to do with LJM and related party transactions, and no mention was made of the Raptors.
context: The Board displaced responsibility for investigating whistleblower concerns by relying on outside counsel's preliminary investigation, which limited its findings to narrow topics.

label: Board members defend approval of LJM as prudent if controlled
original_label: Board members defend approval of LJM as prudent if controlled
quote: Despite these highly unusual features, the Board ratified the code of conduct waiver and approved the LJM1 proposal with little study or debate. Most, in fact, defended the decision to authorize the LJM partnerships and declared that they would support a similar arrangement at another company if appropriate approvals and controls were provided.
context: Board members defended their decision to approve an unprecedented conflict-of-interest arrangement by asserting it would be defensible if controls were in place, implicitly attacking the validity of subsequent criticism.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: Board members unaware of negotiations with Merrill Lynch on LJM2
original_label: Board members unaware of negotiations with Merrill Lynch on LJM2
quote: Enron Board members contend they routinely challenged Enron management proposals, Mr. Fastow had apparently been so confident of Board approval that he had already completed negotiations with Merrill Lynch to develop an LJM2 marketing strategy and had approved an LJM2 private placement memorandum which Merrill Lynch released on October 13, 1999, 1 day after the Board meeting scheduled to approve LJM2's formation. No Board member recalled asking to see or actually reviewing the private placement memorandum or other LJM2 marketing materials, either then or later.
context: Board members deny knowledge or involvement in pre-arranged LJM2 marketing while claiming they made careful decisions, diffusing responsibility by suggesting they were excluded from key information.

category: Appeal to legality and technical compliance
label: Board relies on Andersen as independent auditor giving clean opinion
original_label: Board relies on Andersen as independent auditor giving clean opinion
quote: During the hearing, all five Board witnesses explicitly rejected any share of responsibility for Enron's collapse. One Board member said during his interview that Enron's problem was that Enron management did not tell the truth, and management and Andersen personnel were well aware of the problems and did not tell the Board. When confronted by evidence of Enron's high risk accounting, all of the Board members interviewed by the Subcommittee pointed out that Enron's auditor, Andersen, had given the company a clean audit opinion each year.
context: Board members appeal to Andersen's clean audit opinion as settling the question of accounting propriety, treating auditor approval as legally and morally sufficient.

label: Board dismisses 2 billion in LJM funds flow without inquiry
original_label: Board dismisses 2 billion in LJM funds flow without inquiry
quote: In May 2000, the Finance Committee received a general LJM2 Update reciting the overall benefits that LJM2 had provided to Enron in its first 6 months of operation. This update reported that LJM2 had produced over 2 billion in Funds flow for Enron, over 200 million in Earnings, and 8 days/6 deals/125 million for Enron in the fourth quarter of 1999. Although these figures are remarkable for any new business, there was apparently no discussion of how LJM2 was able to produce such large benefits for Enron in so short a time period.
context: The Finance Committee received extraordinary financial metrics from LJM but failed to inquire into or question how these unusually large benefits were generated, minimizing the red flags.

label: Raptor transactions framed as risk management hedges
original_label: Raptor transactions framed as risk management hedges
quote: The Raptors are a series of four complex transactions that began in mid-2000 and terminated a little over a year later in 2001. They were presented to the Board by Enron management as ingenious accounting devices that might attract accounting scrutiny but had been scrutinized and approved by Andersen. The Powers Report described them as an improper attempt by Enron to use the value of its own stock to offset losses in its investment portfolio, and a highly complex accounting construct that was destined to collapse.
context: Raptor transactions were presented to the Board using euphemistic language as 'ingenious accounting devices' for 'risk management' when they were actually improper attempts to hide losses using Enron stock.

label: Finance Committee assumes annual Raptor updates adequate
original_label: Finance Committee assumes annual Raptor updates adequate
quote: The Subcommittee learned, however, that the Finance Committee subsequently conducted only one quarterly review of LJM transactions, which took place in February 2001. This review was as superficial as that conducted by the Audit Committee. The Finance Committee used the same two-page list of LJM transactions as the Audit Committee and spent about the same amount of time on the document. There was no detailed discussion of the transactions, and no Finance Committee member could recall seeing any DASH or LJM Approval Sheet for any LJM transaction.
context: The Finance Committee displaced responsibility by conducting only one superficial quarterly review despite its stated commitment to quarterly oversight, and relying on summary lists without examining transaction details.

label: Condor vehicle and unconsolidated affiliate structures
original_label: Condor vehicle and unconsolidated affiliate structures
quote: Had they reviewed it, the Board members would have learned that Enron had disclosed in Footnote 16 the existence of the entities on a very limited basis. original_label: Innovation and advancement as corporate purpose

context: Chairman Upton contrasts VW's wrongdoing with the legitimate purpose automakers should pursue, implying that innovation serves a worthy purpose that should not be subordinated to cheating.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: Responsibility spread across organizational levels
original_label: Responsibility spread across organizational levels
quote: There is a lot we still do not know about Volkswagen's actions, or their motivations, in attempting to skirt emissions standards. But regardless of intent, they have betrayed the trust of regulators, dealers and, most importantly, the driving public.
context: Chairman Upton identifies diffuse knowledge and unclear motivations across the company, which could support a defense that responsibility is unclear or distributed rather than concentrated in identifiable decision-makers.

label: Characterization of harm as betrayal rather than environmental impact
original_label: Characterization of harm as betrayal rather than environmental impact
quote: But regardless of intent, they have betrayed the trust of regulators, dealers and, most importantly, the driving public.
context: Chairman Upton frames the wrongdoing primarily in terms of breach of trust rather than quantifying actual environmental or health harm from excess emissions, which allows the moral wrong to be characterized as relational rather than consequential.

label: MCAS deletion from training document
original_label: MCAS deletion from training document
quote: Flight Controls: Delete MCAS, recall we decided we weren't going to cover it [. . .] since it's way outside the normal operating envelope.
context: Boeing employee email to FAA AEG employee on January 17, 2017, regarding the 737 MAX FSB Report, using sanitized language ('Delete,' 'way outside the normal operating envelope') to describe the decision to exclude MCAS from pilot training requirements.

label: FAA approval invoked for FSB report
original_label: FAA approval invoked for FSB report
quote: On or about July 7, 2017, an employee of THE BOEING COMPANY emailed employees of at least two major U.S.-based airline customers, stating in part, 'Attached is the final and approved 737 FSB [R]eport which adds the 737 MAX.'
context: Boeing employee email to airline customers describing the FSB Report as 'approved,' attributing authority to external FAA approval rather than Boeing's own decision-making regarding MCAS disclosure.

label: Defeat device as design feature with switch
original_label: Defeat device as design feature with switch
quote: Volkswagen manufactured and installed software in the electronic control module of these vehicles that sensed when the vehicle was being tested for compliance with EPA emission standards. Put simply, these cars contain software that turns off or significantly reduces the effectiveness of emissions controls when driving normally, and turns them on when the car is undergoing an emission test. Known as a "defeat device," this design feature results in the cars emitting up to 40 times the emissions that are allowed to ensure public health is protected. These devices contain a "switch" that senses whether the vehicle is being tested or not based on various inputs, including the position of the steering wheel, vehicle speed, the duration of the engine's operation, and barometric pressure.
context: EPA Director Grundler explains to Congress what VW software does, using technical sanitized language like "design feature" and "switch" to describe the defeat device mechanism.

label: Critics demonizing the drug itself
original_label: Critics demonizing the drug itself
quote: For example, on May 15, 2007, in an editorial published in the Wall Street Journal, Dr. Sally Satel, a resident scholar at the American Enterprise Institute, wrote that "the real public-health damage here comes from the pitched campaign conducted by zealous prosecutors and public-interest advocates to demonize [OxyContin] itself." Dr. Satel claimed that this prosecution and convictions will only make it harder for pain patients to get treatment and that "this newest injection of malignant hype is the last thing they need."
context: Brownlee reports criticism of the prosecution decision, presenting critics' attacks on prosecutors' motives and competence.

label: Defense bar attacking prosecutorial discretion
original_label: Defense bar attacking prosecutorial discretion
quote: Also, in a paper presented to the American Bar Association, defense attorneys wrote that requiring executives to plead guilty to misdemeanor offenses was unfair and suggested that Congress should consider removing the provision from the statute that holds executives and owners strictly liable for the criminal acts of their companies. In addition, a former U.S. Attorney from the District of Maine wrote a letter to Chief Judge Jones and called our prosecution of the executives "a case of unusual, if not unprecedented, use of prosecutorial discretion."
context: Brownlee reports criticism of the prosecution, presenting defense bar's characterization of prosecutorial decisions as illegitimate.

label: FDA approval as regulatory validation
original_label: FDA approval as regulatory validation
quote: In 1996, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Oxycontin controlled-release tablets for the treatment of moderate to severe, ongoing pain. Oxycontin contains oxycodone HCL, a narcotic with an addiction potential similar to that of morphine. Accordingly, OxyContin is a controlled substance and subject to regulation by the Drug Enforcement Agency. Oxycontin remains an approved prescription drug.
context: Brownlee describes the regulatory framework that enabled OxyContin, though he does not offer this as Purdue's excuse; this is background context.

category: Moral justification and appeal to higher loyalties
label: Market dominance justified by physician demand
original_label: Market dominance justified by physician demand
quote: Purdue also learned from these focus groups that physicians wanted a long lasting pain reliever that was less addictive and less subject to abuse and diversion. Purdue understood that the company that marketed and sold that drug would dominate the pain management market. And that is exactly what Purdue tried to do.
context: Brownlee reports Purdue's internal reasoning from focus groups, showing how Purdue framed market dominance as serving physician preferences for safer pain relief.

category: Appeal to legality and technical compliance
label: Vehicles complied with emissions standards
original_label: Vehicles complied with emissions standards
quote: VW knowingly made or caused to be made false material statements to United States regulators, including the Environmental Protection Agency and the United States Customs and Border Protection, a component of the Department of Homeland Security, stating that the Subject Vehicles complied with applicable United States emissions standards for new motor vehicles, when they did not.
context: The DOJ complaint describes VW's false representations that vehicles met legal standards, showing VW's use of compliance claims as a cover for non-compliance.

category: Moral justification and appeal to higher loyalties
label: Marketing clean diesel to serve customers
original_label: Marketing clean diesel to serve customers
quote: VW represented to its United States customers, United States dealers, and others in the United States that the Subject Vehicles met applicable United States emissions standards and designed a specific marketing campaign to market these vehicles to United States customers as 'clean diesel' vehicles.
context: The DOJ describes VW's framing of the vehicles as environmentally beneficial, suggesting a noble purpose to justify the conduct.

label: Financing vehicles as ordinary collateral
original_label: Financing vehicles as ordinary collateral
quote: VCI offered competitive financing terms by purchasing from dealers certain loans and leases entered into by customers that purchased or leased Volkswagen vehicles, including the Subject Vehicles. VCI also provided financing to VW GoA's authorized dealerships in the United States, called floorplan financing, for Volkswagen vehicles, including the Subject Vehicles. For loans, leases, and floorplan financing, Volkswagen vehicles, including the Subject Vehicles, were the collateral underlying the payment obligations.
context: The DOJ describes VW's financial practices treating the non-compliant vehicles as ordinary collateral, minimizing or normalizing the conduct as routine business.

category: Appeal to legality and technical compliance
label: Compliance with test procedures allowed design choices
original_label: Compliance with test procedures allowed design choices
quote: Mit diesen Prüfbedingungen ist der NEFZ gemeint. Die vom Ausschuss mit einer rechtlichen Begutachtung beauftragten Sachverständigen haben sich auch mit der Reichweite des Abschalteinrichtungsverbots befasst.
english_gloss: These test conditions refer to the NEFZ. The expert witnesses commissioned by the committee to provide legal assessment also addressed the scope of the prohibition on defeat devices.
context: Investigative report explaining how the testing standard (NEFZ) defined the conditions under which emissions had to meet limits, making test compliance a technical matter.

label: European Commission authorized testing procedure changes
original_label: European Commission authorized testing procedure changes
quote: Der europäische Gesetzgeber hat bei Erlass der Grundverordnung im Jahre 2007 berücksichtigt, dass der NEFZ das Fahrverhalten in der Praxis möglicherweise nur begrenzt abbildet. So heißt es in den Erwägungsgründen der Grundverordnung: Es sollten weitere Anstrengungen unternommen werden, [...] um sicherzustellen, dass sich die Grenzwerte auf das tatsächliche Verhalten der Fahrzeuge bei ihrer Verwendung beziehen.
english_gloss: The European legislator took into account when enacting the basic regulation in 2007 that the NEFZ might only partially reflect real-world driving behavior. The recitals of the basic regulation state: Further efforts should be undertaken to ensure that limit values reflect actual vehicle behavior in use.
context: Report explaining how the EU legislative framework acknowledged the NEFZ's limitations but delegated responsibility to the Commission to adapt testing procedures.

label: Technical term obscures defeat device function
original_label: Technical term obscures defeat device function
quote: Ein Konstruktionsteil, das die Temperatur, die Fahrzeuggeschwindigkeit, die Motordrehzahl (UpM), den eingelegten Getriebegang, den Unterdruck im Einlasskrümmer oder sonstige Parameter ermittelt, um die Funktion eines beliebigen Teils des Emissionskontrollsystems zu aktivieren, zu verändern, zu verzögern oder zu deaktivieren, wodurch die Wirksamkeit des Emissionskontrollsystems unter Bedingungen, die bei normalem Fahrzeugbetrieb vernünftigerweise zu erwarten sind, verringert wird.
english_gloss: A structural component that detects temperature, vehicle speed, engine RPM, engaged gear, intake manifold vacuum or other parameters to activate, modify, delay or deactivate the function of any part of the emissions control system, thereby reducing the effectiveness of the emissions control system under conditions that can reasonably be expected in normal vehicle operation.
context: Legal definition of 'Abschalteinrichtung' (defeat device) from the basic regulation, which uses technical and euphemistic language like 'activate, modify, delay or deactivate' rather than plainly stating the device reduces emission control effectiveness.

category: Appeal to legality and technical compliance
label: Compliance with defined test conditions as standard
original_label: Compliance with defined test conditions as standard
quote: Mit Art. 3 Abs. 6 der Durchführungsverordnung erwähnten Prüfbedingungen, unter denen die bei der Emissionsprüfung ermittelten Werte die Grenzwerte nicht überschreiten dürfen, sind in mehreren Anhängen zur Durchführungsverordnung geregelt. Anhang III betrifft die 'Prüfung der durchschnittlichen Abgasemissionen bei Umgebungsbedingungen (Prüfung Typ 1)'. Seine Regelungen verweisen im Wesentlichen auf den in Nr. 5.3.1 der UNECE-Regelung Nr. 83 definierten Rollenprüfstandtest, der gemeinhin als 'Neuer Europäischer Fahrzyklus' bezeichnet wird.
english_gloss: The test conditions mentioned in Article 3(6) of the implementation regulation, under which values determined in emissions testing must not exceed limit values, are regulated in several annexes to the implementation regulation. Annex III concerns 'testing of average exhaust emissions under environmental conditions (Type 1 test)'. Its provisions essentially refer to the chassis dynamometer test defined in No. 5.3.1 of UNECE Regulation No. 83, commonly called the 'New European Driving Cycle'.
context: Report describing how emissions testing regulations established the NEFZ as the legally mandated test procedure, making compliance with it a technical and formal matter.

label: NEFZ limitations acknowledged but treated as known issue
original_label: NEFZ limitations acknowledged but treated as known issue
quote: Schon zu Beginn des Untersuchungszeitraums war bekannt, dass dieser Fahrzyklus, der seine heutige Gestalt in den 1990er Jahren erhalten hatte, das reale emissionsrelevante Fahrverhalten nur noch zum Teil widerspiegelt. So liegt beispielsweise die Maximalgeschwindigkeit im NEFZ bei 120 km/h.
english_gloss: It was already known at the beginning of the investigation period that this driving cycle, which took its current form in the 1990s, only partially reflects real-world emissions-relevant driving behavior. For example, the maximum speed in the NEFZ is 120 km/h.
context: Investigative report noting that limitations of the NEFZ testing cycle were well-known but treated as a routine technical matter rather than a fundamental problem enabling emissions violations.

label: EU Commission given responsibility to monitor and adapt procedures
original_label: EU Commission given responsibility to monitor and adapt procedures
quote: In Art. 14 Abs. 3 der Grundverordnung wird die EU-Kommission dementsprechend zur Beobachtung und, soweit erforderlich, Nachbesserung des gesetzlichen Regelwerkes im Wege des Komitologieverfahrens verpflichtet. Wörtlich heißt es: Die Kommission beobachtet die Verfahren, Prüfungen und Anforderungen nach Art. 5 Absatz 3 sowie die für die Emissionsmessung verwendeten Fahrzyklen.
english_gloss: Accordingly, in Article 14(3) of the basic regulation, the EU Commission is obligated to monitor and, where necessary, improve the statutory regulatory framework through the comitology procedure. It states literally: The Commission shall monitor the procedures, tests and requirements according to Article 5(3) as well as the driving cycles used for emissions measurement.
context: Legal text explaining how responsibility for monitoring and adjusting test procedures was vested in the EU Commission through regulatory procedures, creating distance between manufacturers and oversight.

category: Appeal to legality and technical compliance
label: Regulatory framework treated as settling the question
original_label: Regulatory framework treated as settling the question
quote: Der NEFZ ist nachfolgend graphisch dargestellt: Die Prüfung im NEFZ dauert 19 Minuten und 40 Sekunden und setzt sich aus einem städtischen und einem außerstädtischen Teil mit jeweils genau festgelegtem Zeit-Weg-Profil zusammen. Der Prüfzyklus wird auf dem Rollenprüfstand durchführt. Die Höchstgeschwindigkeit im städtischen Teil beträgt 50 km/h, im außerstädtischen 120 km/h. Die Temperatur der Prüfkammer muss zwischen 20 °C und 30 °C (Thermo- oder Temperaturfenster des NEFZ) liegen.
english_gloss: The NEFZ is shown graphically below: The test in the NEFZ takes 19 minutes and 40 seconds and consists of an urban and an extra-urban part, each with precisely defined time-distance profiles. The test cycle is conducted on the chassis dynamometer. The maximum speed in the urban part is 50 km/h, in the extra-urban part 120 km/h. The test chamber temperature must be between 20°C and 30°C (thermal or temperature window of the NEFZ).
context: Report providing detailed technical specifications of the NEFZ test procedure, presenting compliance with these exact parameters as the regulatory requirement.

label: Manufacturers required to prove compliance through test procedures
original_label: Manufacturers required to prove compliance through test procedures
quote: Nach der Durchführungsverordnung 'weist der Hersteller nach, dass die Fahrzeuge den Prüfanforderungen entsprechen, die in den Anhängen III bis VII, X bis XII, XIV und XVI dieser Verordnung genannt sind.' Im Anhang III ist die Prüfung der Abgase im NEFZ beschrieben, im Anhang XII die Ermittlung der CO2-Emissionen und des Kraftstoffverbrauchs (ebenfalls im NEFZ).
english_gloss: According to the implementation regulation 'the manufacturer proves that the vehicles comply with the test requirements specified in Annexes III to VII, X to XII, XIV and XVI of this regulation.' Annex III describes the test of exhaust gases in the NEFZ, Annex XII the determination of CO2 emissions and fuel consumption (also in the NEFZ).
context: Legal regulation placing the burden on manufacturers to demonstrate compliance through specified test procedures, making the test itself the measure of legality.

category: Appeal to legality and technical compliance
label: Regulatory procedure for type approval as technically sufficient
original_label: Regulatory procedure for type approval as technically sufficient
quote: Auf der Grundlage des Prüfberichts des Technischen Dienstes trifft die Genehmigungsbehörde ihre Entscheidung über die Erteilung der Typgenehmigung. Die EG-Fahrzeuggenehmigungsverordnung sieht die Möglichkeit vor, dass der Hersteller schon mit dem Antrag einen Prüfbericht eines benannten Technischen Dienstes vorlegen kann. In diesem Fall kann das KBA anordnen, dass für den Fahrzeugtyp, für den eine EG-Typgenehmigung beantragt wird, ein entsprechendes Fahrzeug bei ihm oder beim Hersteller vorzuführen ist.
english_gloss: On the basis of the test report from the Technical Service, the approval authority makes its decision on whether to grant type approval. The EG Vehicle Approval Regulation provides for the possibility that the manufacturer can already submit a test report from a designated Technical Service with the application. In this case, the KBA can order that a corresponding vehicle be presented for the vehicle type for which EG type approval is requested, either at the KBA or at the manufacturer's facility.
context: Regulatory framework for type approval based on test reports, treating completion of test procedures as sufficient for granting approval.

category: Appeal to legality and technical compliance
label: Emissions optimization within test cycle is lawful
original_label: Emissions optimization within test cycle is lawful
quote: Die Optimierung auf das Testverfahren stecke im Prinzip auch in der Natur der Genehmigung.
english_gloss: The optimization to the test procedure is basically in the nature of approval/certification.
context: Witness Mönch (UBA) testifies about why the UBA did not treat cycle-specific optimization as illegal manipulation, even when emissions were higher outside the NEFZ.

category: Appeal to legality and technical compliance
label: Emissions control system design within regulatory framework
original_label: Emissions control system design within regulatory framework
quote: In diesen Vorgängen liege eine grundsätzlich zulässige Abstimmung bzw. Optimierung des Emissionskontrollsystems auf die durch das Testverfahren definierten Rahmenbedingungen bzw. eine aus technischer Sicht notwendige Abschalteinrichtung.
english_gloss: These processes involve a fundamentally permissible tuning or optimization of the emission control system to the conditions defined by the test procedure, or a technically necessary shutdown device from a technical perspective.
context: Witness Prof. Hausberger explains that tailoring the emissions control system to test procedure conditions is fundamentally permissible and technically necessary.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: Authorities lack jurisdiction to act
original_label: Authorities lack jurisdiction to act
quote: Das KBA ist eine ausführende Vollzugsbehörde, sie kann nur auf Basis der vorhandenen Rechtsvorschriften agieren (international EG/ECE, national StVZO). Diese sehen ausschließlich Serienüberprüfungen (COP (Conformity of Produktion) bzw. Nachprüfungen) vor. Bislang einzige Ausnahme ist die Feldüberwachung (In-Service-Conformity) gemäß 70/220/EWG i.d.F. 98/69/EG.
context: KBA representatives explain their limited authority to the inter-ministerial working group in September 2008, constraining the scope of the planned field monitoring.

label: Manufacturers responsible for their own field monitoring
original_label: Manufacturers responsible for their own field monitoring
quote: Nach der Richtlinie 98/69/EG die Hersteller selbst eine FÜ (In-Service Conformity) für die von ihnen produzierten Fahrzeuge durchzuführen hätten. Diese Ergebnisse können nach derzeitigem Recht den Zulassungsbehörden mitgeteilt und von diesen überprüft werden. Das KBA macht davon Gebrauch. Nach den Vorschriften der Euro 5/6-Verordnung müssen die Typgenehmigungsbehörden dies zukünftig zwingend tun.
context: KBA representative states the directive places responsibility for field monitoring on manufacturers themselves, with authorities only checking results.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: No detection mechanism available for defeating devices
original_label: No detection mechanism available for defeating devices
quote: Insofern liefere die Abstimmung auf den Zyklus keinen Mechanismus oder keinen konkreten Hinweis, wie so etwas am Fahrzeug erkannt wird, wenn es auf dem Rollenprüfstand steht.
english_gloss: Thus tuning to the test cycle provides no mechanism or concrete indication of how such a thing would be detected on a vehicle when it is on the dynamometer.
context: Witness Mönch (UBA) explains that cycle-specific optimization did not provide evidence or a mechanism for detecting test recognition, justifying why UBA did not investigate further.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: Lack of evidence available for action
original_label: Lack of evidence available for action
quote: Es waren aber zu dem damaligen Zeitpunkt keinerlei Beweise vorhanden. [...] Wir hatten keine direkten Beweise – die hätte man ja nur aus der Automobilindustrie selbst bekommen können –, und wir hatten leider auch keine Vorschläge, wie man eine Beweiskette aufbaut, also eine Untersuchung durchführt, um nachzuweisen, dass solche Einrichtungen im Automobil vorhanden sind. Und ohne einen Vorschlag, wie man das dann nachweisen kann, können Sie nichts nachweisen.
context: Former environment ministry official Prof. Lahl testifies that despite suspicions of cycle beating, they lacked evidence and no methodology existed to prove illegal devices.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: Speculation about whistleblowers but no actual leads
original_label: Speculation about whistleblowers but no actual leads
quote: Ich kann mir – wie gesagt, ich wiederhole mich – nur vorstellen, dass diese Spekulationen aus der Automobilindustrie selber gekommen sind; aber mehr weiß ich nicht.
context: Prof. Lahl speculates that suspicions of cycle beating may have come from industry insiders but admits he has no actual information.

label: Regulatory framework as determinant of test scope
original_label: Regulatory framework as determinant of test scope
quote: Es sollten genau die Testmethoden angewendet werden, die auch im Rahmen der Typgenehmigung geprüft worden sind, sprich: Typ-1-Messungen, Überprüfung der limitierten Schadstoffe. [...] Das Einzige, was [...] wir zusätzlich im Rahmen unseres Feldüberwachungsprojektes mit gemessen haben, das waren die CO2-Emissionen.
context: Witness Dr. Bugsel (BASt) explains the field monitoring project used only the test methods mandated by the regulatory framework for type approval.

category: Appeal to legality and technical compliance
label: Zykluserkennung necessary for legal test operation
original_label: Zykluserkennung necessary for legal test operation
quote: Zudem führte der Zeuge in diesem Kontext aus, dass die Zykluserkennung, also dass das Fahrzeug erkennt, dass es sich in einer Prüfsituation auf dem Rollenprüfstand befindet, in vielen Fällen, bei fast allen modernen Fahrzeugen sogar zwingend erforderlich und daher legal sei. [E]rst wenn die Zykluserkennung zum Zweck der illegalen Emissionsbeeinflussung eingesetzt wird, dann ist sie illegal im Sinne der Vorschrift.
context: Witness Redmann (BMVI) testifies that cycle recognition is legally required in most modern vehicles and only becomes illegal when used to illegally influence emissions.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: Suspicions not substantiated or pursued
original_label: Suspicions not substantiated or pursued
quote: Aber dieser Verdacht ist nie aufgekommen.
context: Witness Redmann states that despite having budget reserves to investigate suspected illegal defeat devices, no such suspicion ever emerged during the field monitoring project.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: Test methodology limits what can be found
original_label: Test methodology limits what can be found
quote: Ziel der Feldüberwachung sei es laut Zeuge Dr. Gail demgemäß gewesen, Fahrzeuge aus dem Feld herauszunehmen [...] und diese dann daraufhin zu untersuchen, ob die noch den Typgenehmigungswerten entsprechen, also den Werten, die ein Fahrzeug zu Beginn seines Lebens hat, wenn es die Typgenehmigung für einen bestimmten Fahrzeugtyp erhält. Um dies machen zu können, muss ich das Fahrzeug natürlich exakt so prüfen, wie ich es auch damals bei der Typgenehmigung gemacht habe. Und wenn ich dies tue, dann finde ich natürlich auch nur diese Sachen heraus, die sich unter den Typgenehmigungsbedingungen abspielen.
context: BASt witness explains that the field monitoring design could only detect issues within type-approval test conditions, structurally limiting its scope.

category: Appeal to legality and technical compliance
label: Regulatory framework determines investigative scope
original_label: Regulatory framework determines investigative scope
quote: Das Problem, vor dem wir als Bundesverkehrsministerium - - oder unser gesamter Geschäftsbereich gestanden hatte, war: Wir können nur auf Basis des geltenden Rechts entsprechende Prüfungen durchführen, das heißt, das Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt kann nur das machen, was entsprechend hinterlegt ist in den Typgenehmigungsvorschriften.
context: Witness Redmann (BMVI) explains that the ministry could only conduct tests within the scope of existing type-approval regulations.

label: Industry sensitivity constrains investigation scope
original_label: Industry sensitivity constrains investigation scope
quote: Da dieses Projekt eine gewisse politische Brisanz besitzt, ist es sinnvoll die enge Zusammenarbeit beizubehalten. Die Brisanz ergibt sich aus der Tatsache, dass die Fahrzeughersteller sehr empfindlich sind, wenn unabhängige Messstellen im Feld befindliche Fahrzeuge vermessen. Um dem vorzubeugen, wird während des Projektes ein Informationsaustausch mit den Herstellern durchgeführt und Transparenz gewährleistet.
context: UBA official Mönch notes in a handover memo that manufacturers' sensitivity about field testing necessitates ongoing communication and transparency.

label: Abweichungen explained by physics not manipulation
original_label: Abweichungen explained by physics not manipulation
quote: Abweichungen im Abgasverhalten außerhalb des NEFZ habe man sich damit erklärt, dass außerhalb des Typprüfzyklus höhere Leistungen aufzubringen seien und insofern auch unter Umständen höhere Emissionen auftreten könnten.
context: Witness Schmidt (TÜV Nord) testifies that emissions deviations outside NEFZ were attributed to higher power requirements, not manipulation.

label: Higher emissions explained by technical necessity
original_label: Higher emissions explained by technical necessity
quote: Allerdings würde er auch den Bericht der Untersuchungskommission Volkswagen mit einem Fragezeichen versehen, da dort letztlich von den Realemissionen auf das Vorhandensein oder Nichtvorhandensein von Abschalteinrichtungen geschlossen werde.
context: Witness Schmied (UBA) questions whether higher real-world emissions necessarily indicate illegal defeat devices, as the report concludes.

label: Higher emissions technically explicable under regulations
original_label: Higher emissions technically explicable under regulations
quote: Es sei völlig erklärbar, dass die höheren Leistungen, die außerhalb des NEFZ abgerufen würden, mit höheren Verbrennungstemperaturen verbunden seien, die wiederum höhere Stickoxidemissionen zur Folge hätten.
context: Witness Schmied explains higher real-world emissions as technically explicable consequences of higher engine loads, not indicating wrongdoing.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: Behörden lacked investigative capability
original_label: Behörden lacked investigative capability
quote: Es gibt verschiedene Begriffe, die im Rahmen dieser ganzen Problematik geäußert werden: Manipulation, Optimierung des Kennfelds, Abschalteinrichtungen. Ich tue mich also mit diesem Begriff Was ist eine Manipulation? extrem schwer, weil ich dafür keine schlüssige Definition habe.
context: Witness Mönch (UBA) testifies about the difficulty of defining manipulation, justifying cautious legal language in field monitoring reports.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: No findings without belastbare Analyse
original_label: No findings without belastbare Analyse
quote: Wenn man dann ganz klar reinguckt: Was habe ich in Berichten dokumentiert, was habe ich an klaren, belastbaren Analysen hinsichtlich solcher Vermutungen, Äußerungen, wie auch immer gesagten Dingen?, dann muss man wirklich sehr bodenständig und sehr solide aufgestellt sein. Insofern muss man da auch unsere Zurückhaltung als Haus verstehen, hinnehmen. Also, man kann nicht Dinge tun als Behörde, als Umweltbehörde, wenn sie nicht auf wirklich guten wissenschaftlichen Unterlagen und Beweisen basieren.
context: Witness Mönch explains UBA's restraint in making findings about defeat devices, citing lack of solid scientific evidence.

label: UBA lacked enforcement powers for compliance
original_label: UBA lacked enforcement powers for compliance
quote: Es endete manchmal in Pattsituationen. Wenn wir also Erklärungen von den Herstellern bekommen, dann können wir diese mit unseren Mitteln nicht widerlegen, dann müssen wir sie auch einfach mal so hinnehmen. [...] rein rechtlich haben wir gar keine Handhabe, sondern es lief wirklich auf eine kooperative Zusammenarbeit mit den Herstellern hinaus.
context: Witness Mönch testifies that UBA had no legal authority to enforce manufacturer compliance with emission control requirements.

category: Appeal to legality and technical compliance
label: Feldüberwachung scope defined by EU directive
original_label: Feldüberwachung scope defined by EU directive
quote: Der Prüfumfang der Messungen sei nach der Richtlinie auf die Ermittlung von Schadstoffemissionen im Typprüfzyklus, also im NEFZ, sowie auf die Ermittlung der Verdunstungsemissionen begrenzt.
context: BMU official Eberhardt notes in a 2008 memorandum that the EU directive limits field monitoring to type-approval-cycle emissions.

label: Manufacturers self-monitor under approved procedure
original_label: Manufacturers self-monitor under approved procedure
quote: Fahrzeughersteller, also nicht das KBA, sind seit dem 01.01.2001 nach EU-Recht zur Durchführung der Feldüberwachung für in Verkehr befindliche Fahrzeuge verpflichtet und vermessen hierzu im Feld befindliche Fahrzeuge. Die Ergebnisse melden die Hersteller dem KBA. Das KBA prüft die Angaben der Hersteller und entscheidet, ob weitere Untersuchungen durchzuführen sind.
context: BMU official Eberhardt describes the regulatory structure in which manufacturers conduct their own field monitoring under KBA review.

category: Diffusion of responsibility and denial of personal involvement
label: UBA had no independent Nachweisverfahren
original_label: UBA had no independent Nachweisverfahren
quote: Was man aber nicht hinbekommen habe, so der Zeuge weiter, sei ein Nachweisverfahren gewesen, um festzustellen, ob diese Technik, also diese Abschalteinrichtungen im Automobil verbaut sind.
context: Prof. Lahl testifies that despite suspicions of defeat devices, no methodology existed to prove their presence in vehicles.

label: Cycle beating as abstract technical possibility
